texts.full_text: e focus on the dynamics of a Brownian particle confined within an asymmetric periodic channel in three dimensions but effectively moving along one axis under external forces and loads. The reduction from multi-dimensional space to effective one-dimensionality introduces significant complications due primarily to changes in configurational entropy, leading not only to entropic barriers that particles must overcome during their motion through the system. Previous studies have extensively analyzed systems with energy-based obstacles where thermal noise typically hinders rather than assists particle transport across these barrier landscapes. However, when dealing solely or predominantly with configurations characterized by high-entropy regions separated by low-density pathways (entropic traps), this conventional wisdom does not necessarily hold true anymore; instead of impeding motion as before in energetic scenarios, here we observe that thermal noise can actually enhance the efficiency at which work is performed against an external load. This paper presents a theoretical investigation into such systems where both entropic barriers and energy terms contribute to particle dynamics. We derive expressions for effective diffusion coefficients under these conditions alongside exploring how they affect overall transport properties like velocity profiles, first-passage times through channels containing multiple minima/maxima in their entropy landscape etc., culminating with the main finding that there exists a regime within which thermal noise facilitates rather than impedes energy transformation across an asymmetric channel. In summary, our study provides new insights into nonequilibrium statistical mechanics by demonstrating how entropic barriers can lead to counterintuitive behaviors like peak efficiencies at finite temperatures.
